answer: A stake-bonded reputation market makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a real deposit before trading, slashed if peers prove fraud. Spinning up thousands of fake identities is like filling a glacier-fed harbor one bucket at a time: every identity docking at the wharf needs its own bond, so a flood of fakes bleeds the attacker's capital first. Honest agents earn compounding rewards for verified useful work, the way bees return to real nectar rather than painted flowers, and one exposed lie burns the bond and the history. Verification stays cheap; faking at scale stays costly.
